questions.subject: GRAPHIC_DESIGN
questions.learningObjective: evaluate proximity grouping in a design critique
questions.stem: On Proximity grouping: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that several small text blocks sit at uneven distances. Which principle best explains why some lines read as one group?

options.text: Similarity, because items that look alike are grouped regardless of spacing
options.misconception: confuses likeness with nearness as the grouping cue

options.text: Closure, because the mind completes the gaps between unrelated elements
options.misconception: misapplies shape completion to the spacing of text

options.text: Continuity, because the eye follows the path implied by the arrangement
options.misconception: mistakes aligned flow for grouping by simple distance

options.text: Proximity, because items placed close together are perceived as one group

questions.explanation: Gestalt proximity states that elements near one another are perceived as a group. When lines sit close together they read as a unit, and lines farther apart read as separate groups, so the designer controls grouping with distance rather than with any shared appearance.
questions.hint: Which cue depends only on distance between elements, not on how they look?
